# University of the Andes (Colombia) — Summary
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes, "Uniandes") was founded in Bogotá in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón as Colombia’s first nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated university, aiming to modernize education and produce technically skilled professionals for national development. Its early model combined both liberal and technical education, influenced by American universities, and fostered international academic collaborations—most notably the three/two program with U.S. universities. Despite Colombia’s political turmoil in its founding years, Uniandes maintained a stance of neutrality and welcomed students and faculty from diverse backgrounds, with rapid growth in academic offerings and innovative approaches to higher education.
The university’s governance is overseen by a Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, Rector (president), vice-rectors, deans, and faculty councils. As of 2022, it comprised 10 faculties and several interdisciplinary centers, supporting academic flexibility and student self-designed curricular programs through interdisciplinary cycles. Uniandes is recognized for its academic excellence, with most faculty holding degrees from top international universities, and 70% of academic staff full-time and PhD-qualified as of 2014. The student population is about 55% male and 45% female, with 30% from outside Bogotá, and a highly selective admissions process—95% of undergraduates were the top 1% of their high school class.
The main campus, located in Bogotá’s historic center, consists of renovated and new buildings, covering 180,551 m², and provides comprehensive facilities including classrooms, laboratories, libraries with over 445,000 books, and extensive sports amenities. Uniandes hosts international students and has exchange agreements with more than 119 universities in 34 countries. Its mascot is a goat named Seneca, symbolizing the university’s spirit. The University of the Andes has produced influential alumni including former Colombian presidents, ministers, scientists, artists, and academics, and is highly esteemed for its contribution to Colombian society and higher education innovation.
